```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

`ms.qc.report` turns the exported results of a targeted MS run into an
HTML QC report for any of the assays **SCFA, AA, BA, TRY and ddhN**. The
report is laid out as an ISO/IEC 17025 record:

1.  **Status**: DRAFT or AUTHORISED, with what is still outstanding
2.  **Report details**: report ID and revision, laboratory, client,
    sample receipt, run, method, instrument, acquisition dates, plate
    order
3.  **Reference materials** and **samples analysed**
4.  **Notes**: deviations, reruns, excluded samples
5.  **QC criteria and decision rule**
6.  **Working range and measurement uncertainty**
7.  **QC summary tables**: PASS / CAUTION for each analyte on each plate
8.  **CAUTION review**: every CAUTION result, the criteria it failed,
    and the decision made
9.  **Analyte plots**
10. **Input data**: each file with its MD5 checksum
11. **Sign-off** and **Software** (package versions and git commit)

## 1. Installation

```{r}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("phenological/ms-qc-report")
library(ms.qc.report)
```

This also installs `fusion` and `ms.parser` from GitHub.

## 2. A first report

The only required arguments are `data` and `assay`:

```{r}
generateReport(
  data        = "~/Downloads/BA_xml/",
  assay       = "BA",
  output_file = "BA_check.html"
)
```

This report will say **DRAFT**: nobody has signed it off and the CAUTION
results have no decisions yet. That is fine for a first look at the run.

To try the package on its example data (two AA plates):

```{r}
generateReport(
  data        = system.file("extdata", package = "ms.qc.report"),
  assay       = "AA",
  output_file = "example_AA.html"
)
```

## 3. A complete report

```{r}
generateReport(
  # the data
  data        = "~/Downloads/BA_xml/",
  assay       = "BA",

  # report details
  title       = "IRMA SRVr015 MS BA",
  output_file = "IRMA_SRVr015_MS_BA.html",
  reportID    = "IRMA_SRVr015_MS_BA_QC_20261110",
  client      = "Dr Client Name",
  contact     = "client@example.com",
  sampleReceivedDate = "2026-10-28",
  project     = "IRMA",
  runID       = "SRVr015",
  methodID    = "v2",
  instrument  = "PAI03",

  # what happened during the run
  notes       = "Plate SRVp002 re-injected after a column change.",
  materials   = c(Calibrants = "CAL-2411", "QC material" = "QC-2410",
                  "Internal standard mix" = "IS-0932"),

  # decisions on CAUTION results (see section 6)
  decisions   = data.frame(
    plate         = c("SRVp001", "SRVp002"),
    analyte       = c("GCA", "TLCA"),
    disposition   = c("Accept", "Re-run"),
    justification = c("Low calibrant excluded per SOP; R2 0.996 after exclusion", NA)
  ),

  # sign-off
  ms_specialist_1 = "YW",
  ms_specialist_2 = "MR",
  ms_lead         = "RK"
)
```

`generateReport()` prints where the report was saved and returns the
path, so you can open it straight away:

```{r}
out <- generateReport(data = "~/Downloads/BA_xml/", assay = "BA")
browseURL(out)
```

### All arguments

| Argument | What to give |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `data` | The data; see section 4. **Required.** |
| `assay` | `"SCFA"`, `"AA"`, `"BA"`, `"TRY"` or `"ddhN"`. **Required.** |
| `fileType` | `"xml"`, `"tsv"` or `"txt"`. Optional: taken from the file extensions. |
| `title` | Title shown at the top of the report. |
| `output_file` | Where to save the report. A bare file name goes in the working directory; `.html` is added if missing. |
| `reportID` | Unique report ID. If left out, one is made from `project`, `runID`, `assay` and today's date, e.g. `IRMA_SRVr015_MS_BA_QC_20261110`. |
| `revision`, `supersedes` | For a reissued report; see section 9. |
| `client`, `contact` | Client name and contact details. |
| `sampleReceivedDate` | Date the samples were received, as `"YYYY-MM-DD"`. |
| `project`, `runID` | e.g. `"IRMA"`, `"SRVr015"`. |
| `methodID` | Method / SOP reference and version. |
| `instrument` | Instrument name or serial number. |
| `notes` | Deviations from the method, reruns, excluded samples, client requests. Shown as "None." if empty. |
| `materials` | Lots / IDs of reference materials, as a named vector or a data frame. |
| `decisions` | Decisions on CAUTION results; see section 6. |
| `uncertainty` | A different working range / uncertainty table for this report; see section 7. |
| `ms_specialist_1`, `ms_specialist_2`, `ms_lead` | Sign-off initials; see section 8. |
| `plateOrder` | The order plates appear in; see section 5. |
| `scale` | `TRUE` (default) plots `log10(value + 1)`; `FALSE` plots raw values. |

Recommended naming:
`projectName_cohortName_sampleMatrixType_runID_MS_assay`, for example
`covid19_biogune_PLA_COVr01_MS_AA.html`.

## 4. The data

Exported files must all be the same type: **all XML, all TSV or all
TXT**. Give them in whichever way is easiest:

```{r}
# a folder: every .xml / .tsv / .txt file in it
data = "~/Downloads/BA_xml/"

# a series of files, e.g. one per plate
data = c("~/exports/SRVp001.xml", "~/exports/SRVp002.xml")

# the same as one comma-separated string
data = "~/exports/SRVp001.xml, ~/exports/SRVp002.xml"

# a wildcard
data = "~/exports/SRVp*.xml"

# a dataElement saved with saveRDS()
data = "~/run/IRMA_SRVr015_MS_BA.rds"

# a dataElement already in your R session (no quotes)
data = IRMA_SRVr015_MS_BA
```

Each file is read with the `ms.parser` reader for the assay (for example
`ms.parser::readBA()`), and the files are combined into one dataElement.
This works even when plates don't all contain the same analytes.

Relative paths are taken from your working directory. On Windows, use
forward slashes (`"C:/Users/username/Desktop/run"`) or double
backslashes (`"C:\\Users\\username\\Desktop\\run"`).

### Which analytes are reported

-   **Internal standards** (names containing `[IS]`) are never reported.
-   **BA**: only the bile acids listed in `BA_names` (in
    `R/Constants.R`). `ms.parser` names bile acids like
    `CDCA-Chenodeoxycholic acid`; the report shows the abbreviation,
    `CDCA`.
-   **AA, TRY, ddhN, SCFA**: every analyte, with names exactly as in the
    data (e.g. `1-methylhistidine`).

## 5. Plate order

The tables and every plot use the same plate order:

1.  the order you give, e.g. `plateOrder = c("SRVp002", "SRVp001")`.
    Plates you leave out are added at the end, and a name that isn't in
    the data gives a warning;
2.  otherwise by each plate's earliest Acquisition Date, if every plate
    has one;
3.  otherwise by plate name, in natural order (`COVp2` before `COVp10`).

The order used is recorded under Report details and under each plot.

## 6. QC criteria and CAUTION decisions

An analyte is **PASS** on a plate only if all three criteria are met:

| Metric | Criterion | Samples used |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| `R2` | ≥ 0.99 | calibration |
| `totalQCPassPerc` | ≥ 66% of QC injections with Accuracy/Recovery between 80% and 120% | `qc` |
| `LTR_RSD` | ≤ 20% | `ltr` (`pqc` for SCFA, shown as `PQC_RSD`) |

The analyte is **CAUTION** if any criterion fails, or if one can't be
calculated: no R2 reported, no QC injections on the plate, or fewer than
two LTRs. A QC injection with no accuracy value counts as a fail. Values
equal to a limit meet it.

The limits are set once, in `QC_CRITERIA` in `R/Constants.R`. The
summary tables, the cell colours and the criteria printed in the report
all use them, so they always agree.

### Recording decisions

CAUTION is not a release decision. The **CAUTION review** section lists
every CAUTION result with the criteria it failed, for example:

| Plate | Analyte | Failed criteria |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| JUVp003 | Isoleucine | LTR RSD 25.99% \> 20% |
| PLASMA8B | Homocysteine | R2 0.8915 \< 0.99; QC pass 46.15% (6/13) \< 66%; LTR RSD not calculable (\< 2 values) |

The reviewer records a decision for each one in `decisions`:

```{r}
decisions = data.frame(
  plate         = c("JUVp003", "PLASMA8B"),
  analyte       = c("Isoleucine", "Homocysteine"),
  disposition   = c("Accept", "Re-run"),
  justification = c("Not in client panel; reported for information only", NA)
)
```

-   `disposition` is `"Accept"`, `"Re-run"` or `"Reject"`.
-   `"Accept"` needs a `justification`; without one the report stops
    with a message.
-   Plate and analyte names must match the CAUTION review exactly. A
    decision that matches no CAUTION result is listed in the status box.

A practical way to work: make the report once without `decisions`, copy
the plate and analyte names from the CAUTION review, then add the
decisions and make it again.

## 7. Working range and measurement uncertainty

By default the report shows the package table for the run's assay, kept
as a CSV file in the package:

```         
inst/uncertainty/AA.csv
inst/uncertainty/BA.csv
```

Each file has one row per analyte:

```         
analyte,LLOQ,ULOQ,units,U_percent
1-methylhistidine,1,400,µM,
Alanine,1,400,µM,
```

| Column | Meaning |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `analyte` | Exactly as in the data: `1-methylhistidine`, not `1-Methylhistidine`. For BA, the abbreviation (`CDCA`). |
| `LLOQ`, `ULOQ` | Working range of the method. |
| `units` | e.g. `µM`, `nM`. |
| `U_percent` | Expanded measurement uncertainty, %, k = 2. |

The report shows only the analytes in the run. It lists any analyte that
has no entry, and says so if `U_percent` is empty. Both also appear as
notes in the status box, so a name mismatch can't go unnoticed.

**To change the table for every future report**, edit the CSV in Excel
(save as CSV UTF-8) and reinstall the package. **To add an assay**, add
a file named after it, e.g. `inst/uncertainty/TRY.csv`.

**To use a different table for one report**, give a CSV file or a data
frame:

```{r}
generateReport(data = "~/Downloads/BA_xml/", assay = "BA",
               uncertainty = "~/Documents/BA_uncertainty_2026.csv")

generateReport(data = "~/Downloads/BA_xml/", assay = "BA",
               uncertainty = data.frame(analyte = c("CDCA", "GCA"),
                                        LLOQ = 2.5, ULOQ = 1000, units = "nM",
                                        U_percent = c(8.4, 9.1)))
```

## 8. Sign-off and report status

| Role              | Responsibility                     |
|-------------------|------------------------------------|
| `ms_specialist_1` | Data processed and report prepared |
| `ms_specialist_2` | QC results independently reviewed  |
| `ms_lead`         | Report authorised for release      |

Initials must be 2–4 letters (`"yw"` is stored as `"YW"`). The status
box notes it if the same initials appear in more than one role.

The report is **DRAFT** until it has:

-   a report ID,
-   all three sign-off initials,
-   a decision for every CAUTION result, and
-   for a revised report, the ID of the report it supersedes.

It then shows **AUTHORISED**. The status box also notes, without
blocking, if the package was run from source with uncommitted changes.

A typical workflow:

1.  MS specialist 1 makes the report with their initials and checks it.
2.  MS specialist 2 reviews the CAUTION results, agrees the decisions,
    and the report is made again with `decisions` and their initials.
3.  The MS Lead adds their initials and makes the final, AUTHORISED \#

## 9. Reissuing a report

Give the new report a revision number and the ID of the report it
replaces:

```{r}
generateReport(
  data       = "~/Downloads/BA_xml/", assay = "BA",
  reportID   = "IRMA_SRVr015_MS_BA_QC_20261117",
  revision   = 1,
  supersedes = "IRMA_SRVr015_MS_BA_QC_20261110",
  notes      = "Revision 1: GCA on SRVp002 re-run and now within criteria.",
  output_file = "IRMA_SRVr015_MS_BA_rev1.html"
)
```

## 10. Using the template as a notebook

Instead of calling `generateReport()`, you can copy the template, fill
it in and knit it:

```{r}
file.copy(system.file("rmarkdown/templates/reportTemplate.Rmd", package = "ms.qc.report"),
          "IRMA_SRVr015_MS_BA_QC.Rmd")
```

-   Report details, sign-off, `notes:` and `uncertainty:` are in the
    YAML header. In RStudio, **Knit \> Knit with Parameters...** shows
    them as a form.
-   The laboratory, reference materials and CAUTION decisions are in the
    `edit-here` chunk at the top.
-   Knitted from inside the `ms.qc.report` source folder, the template
    loads the package from source with `devtools::load_all()`; the
    Software section then records the git commit. Anywhere else it uses
    the installed package.

## 11. Using the functions directly

```{r}
library(fusion)
dae <- parseMS(folder = "~/Downloads/BA_xml/", assay = "BA", fileType = "xml")

tables <- summaryTables(dae, plateOrder = NULL)
tables$data$SRVp001     # metrics for one plate
tables$tables$allPlates # LTR RSD across all plates
tables$note             # how the plates were ordered

plots <- plotQC(dae, scale = TRUE)
plots[["CDCA"]]
```

## 12. Troubleshooting

| Message | Cause and fix |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `assay must be one of ...` | Check the spelling; it is case-sensitive (`"ddhN"`, not `"DDHN"`). |
| `Data not found: ...` | Check the path. On Windows use `/` or `\\`, not a single `\`. |
| `No matching files found in: ...` | The folder has no files of that type; check `fileType`. |
| `All files must be the same type` | The files are a mix of XML / TSV / TXT. |
| `No QC data to report ...` | No analytes with `qc` and `ltr` (or `pqc`) samples were found. |
| `plateOrder contains plate(s) not in the data` | A name in `plateOrder` doesn't match a plate ID. |
| `A justification is required to accept ...` | Add a `justification` for every `"Accept"` in `decisions`. |
| `disposition must be "Accept", "Re-run" or "Reject"` | Check the spelling in `decisions`. |
| `` `ms_lead` must be initials `` | Use 2–4 letters. |
| `A reissued report ... needs supersedes` | Give the ID of the report this one replaces. |
| `` `sampleReceivedDate` must be a date as "YYYY-MM-DD" `` | e.g. `"2026-10-28"`. |
| Status note: *analyte(s) have no working range / uncertainty entry* | Add rows to the CSV, with names exactly as in the data. |
